challenges.name: find-the-render-loop-evidence
challenges.title: Find the Render Loop: read the evidence
challenges.description: Since Friday's release every catalog tab sends GET /courses?category=react&page=1 about 40 times a second until the rate limiter answers 429. Six statements on one evidence pack - the release diff (A), the Network panel (B), the React DevTools Profiler (C) and the API log (D) - take you from reading the evidence to a hypothesis, past two wrong explanations, to the fix and its verification.

questions.question:
Evidence C - React DevTools Profiler, local reproduction (npm run dev), "Record why each component rendered" enabled:
Commit  Component    Why did this render?
41      CourseList   Hook 2 changed
42      CourseList   Hooks 1 and 2 changed
43      CourseList   Hook 2 changed
44      CourseList   Hooks 1 and 2 changed
...
CatalogPage (the parent of CourseList) did not render during the recording.
(Hook 1 = the courses state, Hook 2 = the loading state.)

Statement: "CourseList keeps rendering because its own state changes, not because CatalogPage re-renders it with new props."
questions.explanation: True. Every commit in C names a hook of CourseList as the reason (Hook 2 = loading, Hooks 1 and 2 = courses and loading), none says "Props changed" or "The parent component rendered", and the parent did not render at all. So the cycle is closed inside CourseList: its own state updates cause the renders. This matters because it rules out a whole family of fixes, such as memoizing the parent or wrapping CourseList in memo. The common mistake is to assume a component that renders too often is always pushed by its parent.

questions.question:
Evidence B - Network panel, production (https://app.codedev.test/catalog?category=react), one tab:
Name                            Status  Started    Time   Initiator
courses?category=react&page=1   200     0.000 s    22 ms  CourseList.tsx:12
courses?category=react&page=1   200     0.024 s    19 ms  CourseList.tsx:12
courses?category=react&page=1   200     0.047 s    23 ms  CourseList.tsx:12
courses?category=react&page=1   200     0.072 s    21 ms  CourseList.tsx:12
... about 2,000 more rows with the same URL ...
courses?category=react&page=1   429     50.310 s   3 ms   CourseList.tsx:12

Evidence D - API access log (api.codedev.test, one user):
14:02:07.112 GET /courses?category=react&page=1 200 4ms user=u_8812 build=2026.10.23-1
14:02:07.136 GET /courses?category=react&page=1 200 3ms user=u_8812 build=2026.10.23-1
14:02:07.159 GET /courses?category=react&page=1 200 4ms user=u_8812 build=2026.10.23-1
...
14:02:57.422 GET /courses?category=react&page=1 429 0ms user=u_8812 limit=2000/min

Statement: "The backend is too slow: requests pile up while earlier ones are still waiting, so a timeout on fetchCourses would stop the flood."
questions.explanation: False. D shows the server answering in 3-4 ms, and B shows about 20 ms end to end, with each request starting only after the previous one has finished (0.000 s + 22 ms, next at 0.024 s). Nothing is piling up and no request waits long enough for a timeout to fire. The requests are sent because each completed response leads to the next one; a faster backend would make the loop spin faster. The misconception is to read "many requests" as "slow requests"; the 429 is the rate limiter reacting to the loop, not its cause.

Evidence D - API access log (api.codedev.test, one user):

14:02:07.136 GET /courses?category=react&page=1 200 3ms user=u_8812 build=2026.10.23-1
14:02:07.159 GET /courses?category=react&page=1 200 4ms user=u_8812 build=2026.10.23-1
...
14:02:57.422 GET /courses?category=react&page=1 429 0ms user=u_8812 limit=2000/min

Statement: "This is React StrictMode running the effect twice in development; the production build sends one request per visit."
questions.explanation: False. StrictMode's extra setup and cleanup happens only in development and only once per mount, so it explains at most two requests on mount. B and D come from production (build 2026.10.23-1 on app.codedev.test) and show about 2,000 identical requests in 50 seconds from one tab. The misconception is to dismiss repeated effects as StrictMode without counting them: StrictMode doubles once, a loop never stops.

True. This is the cycle, and it explains all the evidence. Diff A moves the object literal { category, page } into the render body and makes it the only dependency. React compares dependencies with Object.is, which compares objects by identity, so a fresh object never equals the previous one, even with the same category and page. C shows the two halves of each turn: setLoading(true) in the effect (Hook 2), then setCourses and setLoading(false) when the response arrives (Hooks 1 and 2). Before the release the dependencies were a string and a number, compared by value, so the cycle stopped after one request.

False. An empty array stops the loop because the effect then runs only on mount, but for the same reason it never runs again when category or page changes: page 2 would keep showing page 1. A fix must meet every requirement of the component: one request on mount, one per real change of category or page, none on a same-props re-render, and the spinner during a request. The fix that does that makes the effect depend on the values that define the request and compare by value. The misconception is to judge a fix only by whether the symptom stops.

True. On the shipped code the effect fires again after every render, so the count is already above 1 before the first assertion and the test fails. After a correct fix, the same-props re-render sends nothing and the page change sends exactly one request. The test also catches the tempting wrong fix: with an empty dependency array the page 2 step stays at 1 call and fails. Counting requests is the same evidence as the Network panel in B, made automatic; "the page looks right" is not, because the shipped page also looked right for a few seconds.

challenges.name: find-the-render-loop
challenges.title: Find the Render Loop
challenges.description: Since Friday's release the CodeDev catalog page never stops loading: the API logs show GET /courses?category=react&page=1 about 40 times a second from every open tab and the rate limiter starts answering 429. The release only moved the request parameters of CourseList into a query object. Fix CourseList so that it requests the courses once on mount, once more each time category or page changes, and never when its parent re-renders it with the same props, while still showing "loading" during a request. The file contains a small hook runtime that follows React's rules (effects run after the render when a dependency changed by Object.is); the test runner mounts the component and prints the requests and the screen after each step.
hints: The effect runs whenever one of its dependencies is not Object.is-equal to the value from the previous render. Is `query` ever equal to the previous `query`?
Look at the line that builds `query` and at the dependency array of the effect. Follow one request: it resolves, setCourses and setLoading run, the component renders again - what does the effect see?

A similar case: `const options = { sort: 'title' }; useEffect(() => load(options), [options]);` reloads after every render. Depending on `options.sort` (a string) instead, and building the object inside the effect, makes the effect run only when the sort really changes.
